findings.title: No test for rounding with amounts that don't divide evenly
findings.explanation: The PR says it covers a partial month, but 3000 over 30 days gives a whole number of units per day, so the test never exercises rounding. The 10-day case is also essentially the existing mid-period test with different numbers. Add a case such as 1000 over 30 days after 10 days (666.67 exact) and assert the intended rounding behaviour (round, floor or ceil). Money rounding is the usual source of proration bugs. If the implementation uses floating-point division, also confirm that `toBe(2000)` is exact and not 1999.999...

findings.title: Test name and PR description don't match what is tested
findings.explanation: The PR describes a 'partial month', but the test uses a full 30-day period (April 1 to May 1) and a whole number of days. A genuine partial-period or mid-day case, for example a cancellation at 12:00 or a 31-day month, would match the description better. Otherwise rename the test and update the description.

findings.title: Two scenarios per test case
findings.explanation: Each of the first two new tests asserts both the boundary case (equal to start or end) and the out-of-range case in a single `it`. If the first assertion fails, the second never runs, and the failure message does not say which scenario broke. Splitting them, or using `it.each`, gives clearer diagnostics.

findings.title: Other edge cases not covered
findings.explanation: Consider adding tests for degenerate input such as `end <= start` (zero-length or inverted period, which risks division by zero or NaN), a zero amount, and a period crossing a DST change or a leap day if the implementation uses local dates. These can be follow-ups, but they are the edge cases most likely to cause production bugs.

Covers cancellations at the start and end of a period, before it starts, after it ends, and a partial month.
